newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH FLOWER WHOLESALERS TURNOVER +12.1 PCT IN H1.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH FLOWER WHOLESALERS TURNOVER +12.1 PCT IN H1.

text.p: Dutch flower and plant wholesalers and producers have experienced a 12.1 percent growth in turnover for the first half of the year, compared to the same period last year, BGB, the Dutch association of producers and wholesalers, said in a statement.
Turnover increased to 4.4 billion guilders for the first half. The increase is nearly twice as much as it was in 1996, when the rise was 6.8 percent.
Overall, for the first half, the sale of bulbs and cuttings increased by 17.1 percent to around 200 miliion guilders.
Plant sales went up by 14 percent to 1.3 billion guilders and cut flowers increased by 11 percent to 2.9 billion.
The BGB said its main export market, Germany, had fallen behind the average growth rate, whereas the UK had bought 30 percent more from the Dutch association members.
Italy bought 27 percent more and Belgium 22 percent more.
Exports also increased to the former Eastern bloc countries, especially Russia and Poland, said a BGB spokesman.
Germany, the association's largest export market, saw a 2.5 percent decline in market share for the first six months, to 45.1 percent share.
The dip in sales to Germany was blamed on a weaker German economy and the fact that there was a lower demand for cut flowers.

There is also a shift towards more direct imports from countries such as Israel, Kenya and Zimbabwe into Germany, the BGB stated. Southern Germans also buy flowers and plants from southern European countries.
However, for plants it was more positive. Germans bought 11.4 percent more plants in the first six months than in the same period last year.

The UK, however, presented a different picture because of the strength of the pound sterling. The UK bought 30 percent more flowers and plants (89 million guilder worth) from the Dutch. In June alone, the British bought 44 percent more.
The exporters said it was not only the strength of the pound but the increased assortment of flowers, special products and better quality, which led to the increase.

Exports to Russia increased in the first half by 90 percent to 85 million guilders. Poland bought 74 percent more (to 39 million guilders) and The Czech Republic bought 28 percent more (to 27 million guilders).
Despite the high growth, eastern bloc country sales account for only six percent of the Dutch market sales.
In the month of June, 575 million guilders worth of flowers and plants were bought, an increase of 15.8 percent on May. Exports increased by eight percent in May this year.

Generally, average prices were a lot higher, the BGB said, despite the fact that there was no shortage in capacity. But increased international competition meant that Dutch exporters have to put more effort into improving quality and offering more variety of flowers and plants, the assocation warned.
